correctness.rationale: For u with maximal runs c_i^ell_i and source-run capacities a,b, greedily embedding in (0^a1^b)^m yields last occupied host run J(u)=1_{first run is 1}+(h−1)+2 sum_i(ceil(ell_i/d_i)−1); u is present iff J(u)<=2m−1. The per-run inequality 2(ceil(ell/d)−1)<=ell−1 for d>=2 has equality exactly at odd ell for d=2, and ell=1 for d>=3. Hence when a,b>=2, shortest absent length 2m and words starting with 1 having exactly those run restrictions, with counts F_{2m}, 2^(m−1), or 1. If capacity one, shortest absent length m+1 and explicit two-word boundary (or m+2 alternating list). Independent brute-force checks for all a,b=1..4 and m=1..4 confirmed five counts and no shorter absence. These are mathematically sound but are already a shortest-length layer of a published complete minimal-absent language theorem.
